text: I've overseen the canal terraces since my father's knees gave out.
The river's course shifted gradually across several dry years, not overnight.
I remember replanting the lower terraces three times in one bad stretch because the water simply wasn't reaching them anymore.
Two of my upper terraces now flood unevenly compared to twenty years ago.
I believe the river is still drifting, just slower now than during the Turning itself.
Mara wants more seed-grain held back than I think the terraces can spare.
We settle it every season, though neither of us is fully satisfied.
Noki reads the gate schedules faster than I did at her age.
She'll run these terraces well after I can't.
We grow cotton for trade cloth, but I've cut the cotton acreage twice to protect the grain fields.
Sena's weaving guild wants more raw cotton than I can safely spare some seasons.
She understands when I say no, even if she doesn't like it.
Ren once asked me whether the old field boundary stones matched the current terrace lines.
They don't, not exactly. The lines have shifted along with the water.
I no longer trust the old planting calendar exactly as written.
I've quietly adjusted my own sowing dates a few days earlier each year.
The archive-keeper asked about old terrace maps once.
I showed her what I had. She seemed to already suspect what I found.
Some low terraces near the Old Canal Bed haven't produced well in years. I keep farming them out of stubbornness, not sense.
